takeaway: Epistaxis with normal observations: first nasal compression and sucking an ice cube. Packing, cautery and ENT referral come later if bleeding persists.

question.text: A 55-year-old man has epistaxis with normal observations. Which management should be undertaken first?

answer.text: Sucking on an ice cube and compression

lines.text: A nosebleed, but his observations are completely normal.
The monitor looks healthy, so after the ABC check nothing more urgent needs fixing.
So the first step is simple first aid: pinch the soft part of the nose and suck an ice cube.
lines.say: (laugh) So the first step is simple first aid: pinch the soft part of the nose and suck an ice cube.

lines.text: Steady nasal compression is what stops most nosebleeds.
Only if it keeps bleeding do we move on. Nasal packing gives tamponade.
If the bleeding point is visible with little blood loss, cautery is possible.
Specialist steps like ENT referral wait behind the door.
So: ice cube sucking and compression comes first.
